variants.prompt: The end wall of a commercial greenhouse is a rectangle $16$ m wide and $5$ m tall, topped by an isosceles triangular gable on the same base. Each sloping edge of the gable measures $10$ m. A circular exhaust fan opening of radius $2$ m is cut out of the wall. Using $\pi = 3.14$, how many square meters of glazing cover the remaining wall? Give the answer in square meters, rounded to two decimal places.
variants.inputHint: Enter a decimal rounded to two decimal places
variants.checkpointHint: The sloping gable edge is the hypotenuse of a right triangle formed with half the wall width and the vertical gable height.
variants.figureWaiver: The vertical gable height is derived from the sloping edge; a labeled facade figure would give it away.

steps.explain: Halve the base width to get the horizontal leg of the right triangle inside the gable.
Apply the Pythagorean theorem with the sloping edge as the hypotenuse.
Square the sloping edge and the half-base.
Subtract to find the square of the gable height.
Take the positive square root to obtain the gable height.
Set up the area of the rectangular wall.
Multiply the width and height of the rectangle.
Set up the area of the triangular gable using the derived vertical height.
Evaluate the area of the triangular gable.
Set up the area of the circular exhaust fan opening.
Square the radius and multiply by pi.
Add the rectangular wall and gable areas, then subtract the circular cut-out.
Compute the net glazing area.

variants.prompt: A cylindrical dairy holding tank holds $226.08$ m$^3$ and is $8$ m tall. Only its curved vertical side will be coated with thermal sealant. Each bucket of sealant covers $12$ m$^2$, and sealant is sold only in whole buckets. Using $\pi = 3.14$, how many buckets must be purchased?
variants.inputHint: Enter a whole number of buckets
variants.checkpointHint: Back-solve the radius from the volume first, multiply the full circumference by the height for the curved surface area, and round up to whole containers.
variants.figureWaiver: The radius is derived from the tank capacity; a labeled cylinder figure would give it away.

steps.explain: Substitute capacity and height into the cylinder volume formula.
Multiply pi by the height.
Divide both sides by the coefficient of the squared radius.
Take the positive square root to find the radius.
Write the lateral surface area of the curved side using the derived radius.
Evaluate the curved surface area.
Divide the curved surface area by the coverage per bucket.
Round up to the next whole bucket so the entire curved side is covered.

blindSolve.edgeRejected: r = -3 (non-physical negative radius) and 12 buckets (12*12 = 144 m^2 < 150.72 m^2, insufficient sealant).

steps.explain: Apply the Pythagorean theorem with the roof slant edge as hypotenuse.
Square the slant edge and radius.

Write the conical roof volume using the derived vertical height.
Evaluate the volume of the conical roof.
Set the sum of cylinder volume and cone volume equal to the total capacity.
Divide by pi and subtract the cone coefficient from the total.
Divide by the squared radius to find the cylindrical height.
